details.publicNotes:
A theater production can be a stressful process for all involved. Tempers flare, egos clash, and anger simmers. These powerful emotions can resonate within the everyday props that are frequently exposed to them. On rare occasions, this resonance develops its own sentience and ego.

Amphitwisters only occur in venues that have hosted hundreds of performances, manifesting on the night of a particularly ambitious or fevered performance. While they are not actively malicious, amphitwisters underestimate the damage their rampages can cause. After all, an actor who dies a bloody death on stage rises to perform another night, so why should it be any different for the people left bleeding on the ground in the wake of an amphitwister's excitable tempest? In a fight, amphitwisters careen wildly throughout the venue, darting into range to whip costumes, props, and dangerous shards of glass at their foes. Despite their theatrical origin, they show no preference or animosity toward bards or other thespians.

Once defeated, the amphitwister dissipates, leaving behind a manifested crystal of psychic energy. This valuable keepsake is infused with the resonance of the theatrics that shaped it and makes an excellent ingredient for crafting magical costumes and instruments.

Everyone's a Critic

Even when they are not physically manifested, amphitwisters are aware of the goings-on in their theater and never miss a performance. They often develop strong feelings about members of an acting troupe, selecting beloved darlings who must be preserved at all costs and labeling others as talentless hacks who should be driven from the theater, with violence if necessary. When an amphitwister appears, they are always forthcoming with their opinions, with their words often as cutting as their attacks.

Trigger A creature within 30 feet would use an action with the emotion trait

Effect The amphitwister detests interruptions to the show, whether they be Demoralizing hecklers or people spinning magic to take control of the narrative. The triggering creature must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:30] save or the triggering action is disrupted.

The amphitwister envelops all creatures in its space in an array of comically mismatched clothing. All creatures in its space must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:27] save to avoid being costumed.

@UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.effects.Item.0gOoTjhJjMRmtzUB]{Effect: Fashion Disaster}

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature takes a –15-foot status penalty to their Speeds and a –2 circumstance penalty to Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, and Performance checks until they [[/act escape dc=27]] the clothing.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} until they remove the clothing.

The swarm ejects a storm of mirror shards. All creatures in a @Template[type:burst|distance:15] within 120 feet of the swarm take @Damage[(4d6+9)[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:27|basic] save).

The amphitwister's props arrange themselves, gathering into four adjacent squares. This reduces the swarm's size to Large but increases the damage of its Prop Barrage to 3d12. The swarm remains Large until it spends another action with the move trait to disperse to its original size.
Each foe in the swarm's space takes @Damage[3d8[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:30|basic]).
